newsitem.title: TAIWAN: S.Korean crackdown slashes Taiwan gold imports.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean crackdown slashes Taiwan gold imports.

text.p: Taiwan's gold bullion imports from South Korea plunged 82 percent in August from July as Seoul regulators cracked down on speculative gold trade, officials and traders said on Monday.
Taiwan imported just 270 kg of gold bullion from South Korea in August, down from 1,500 kg in July, Finance Ministry data showed.

The August total contrasted even more sharply with Taiwan's 1,929 kg average monthly gold imports from South Korea over the first seven months of the year, when a complex gold speculation scheme based on international interest-rate arbitrage was in full swing.
Taiwan gold bullion imports from South Korea soared in the first seven months as South Korean bullion houses used the island to park their speculative gold positions, traders said.
The South Korean government cracked down on the practice on July 1, and gold exports plunged as new rules took the profits out of the scheme, traders said.
In the scheme, Taiwan was one of the markets used as a dumping ground for gold positions that South Korean traders bought through complicated interest-rate arbitrage arrangements.

Typically, South Korean bullion houses were importing large amounts of gold bullion on 90-day deferred payments, then immediately exporting the gold and parking the proceeds in high interest-bearing South Korea money market instruments.
Significant profits could be earned by exploiting the gap between South Korea's interest rates of more than 11 percent and London's Interbank Offered Rate of about five percent.
In the crackdown, South Korea shortened the deferred payment period to a maximum of 30 days, chilling what had been a booming gold transshipment business.
